description: ECG changes associated with electrolyte imbalances
overview: This module covers ECG manifestations of hyperkalemia, hypokalemia, hypercalcemia, and hypocalcemia, focusing on recognition and clinical significance.
objectives: Learn emergency management of electrolyte abnormalities

slides.title: Hyperkalemia
slides.content: Hyperkalemia progression: peaked T waves → PR prolongation → P wave disappearance → QRS widening → sine wave pattern → asystole. Immediate treatment required.

slides.title: Hypokalemia
slides.content: Hypokalemia: flattened T waves, ST depression, prominent U waves, QT prolongation, arrhythmias. May precipitate torsades de pointes.

quiz.question: What is the characteristic ECG finding in hypokalemia?
quiz.explanation: Prominent U waves are characteristic of hypokalemia.

slides.title: Calcium Abnormalities
slides.content: Hypercalcemia: short QT interval. Hypocalcemia: prolonged QT interval, may lead to torsades de pointes. Calcium affects primarily the ST segment and QT interval.

quiz.question: What ECG change is associated with hypercalcemia?
quiz.explanation: Hypercalcemia is associated with shortened QT interval.

slides.title: Emergency Management
slides.content: Emergency management: assess severity, correct underlying cause, specific treatments (calcium gluconate for hyperkalemia, potassium replacement for hypokalemia), continuous monitoring.

quiz.question: What is the first-line treatment for severe hyperkalemia?
quiz.explanation: Calcium gluconate is first-line treatment for severe hyperkalemia to stabilize myocardium.
